# The counting-protocol review — what to do, in order

**Built 2026-10-18.** Generated by `code/make_protocol_review.py`.

## What this is settling

Three protocols have been used to say how many surfers are in a frame, and they
disagree enough to have blocked three separate detection changes. On the frames
where they overlap:

| | vs CVAT box count | n | frames below / above | p |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| `reviewdays` (box-by-box, TP + missed) | **+0.27** | 11 | 5 / 5 | 0.74 |
| `spotcheck` (direct `my_count`) | **−3.27** | 15 | **14 / 0** | **0.0001** |

So the direct count reads about **11% low**, flat across crowd levels, and that
single bias is enough to flip `spotcheck` from rejecting the crowd-dependent
detection rules to endorsing them.

What it does **not** settle is which protocol is right. CVAT annotation and
`reviewdays` share a *mode* of looking — slow, magnified, box-assisted — even
though they share neither frames nor task. So the 11% is either real surfers a
glance misses, or marginal blobs that close looking manufactures. Every frame
that has a careful count was counted carefully, so the existing data cannot
separate those.

This review counts the **same fresh frames twice**, once each way.

## Pass A — direct count, first and unprimed

30 frames in `pass_a_direct_count/`, clean crops at 2×, no boxes drawn, no
detector count shown, shuffled so the filenames do not order by crowd.

For each image fill one row of `pass_a.csv`:

- `my_count` — how many surfers you count. One pass, the way you would answer
  "how many people are out there right now."
- `my_ci_plusminus` — your own ± uncertainty on that number.
- `notes` — anything unusual (fog, glare, an unusable frame → write `na`).

**Do not zoom beyond what the image gives you, and do not revisit a frame after
moving on.** The point of this pass is to reproduce the `spotcheck` mode, which
is a direct count of the scene. If you count it carefully here, both passes
measure the same thing and the review returns nothing.

## Pass B — box-by-box, only after A is returned

Generated by `python code/make_protocol_review.py --pass b`, which **refuses to
run until `pass_a.csv` has counts in it**. Same 30 frames, reshuffled into a
different order, production boxes drawn and numbered.

- `pass_b_boxes.csv` — one row per box, `is_surfer` = `y`/`n`.
- `pass_b_missed.csv` — one row per frame, `surfers_with_no_box` = how many real
  surfers carry no box at all.

Truth under this protocol is `(boxes marked y) + surfers_with_no_box`, matching
how `reviewdays` was built. Take as long as you like and zoom freely — that is
the mode being tested.

**The two passes must be separated.** If both sheets are open at once the second
anchors on the first and the paired difference, which is the whole measurement,
collapses toward zero. Pass B is deliberately not generated up front for that
reason.

## Why 30, and why these 30

Six frames from each of five crowd strata by production count (0–2, 3–9, 10–19,
20–34, 35+), drawn from the current model era so pass B shows the boxes
production actually emits, and excluding every frame already in `reviewdays`,
`spotcheck` or the CVAT splits — so neither pass is a re-count of something
already seen.

Paired, two-sided, α 0.05: **n = 30 detects a mean protocol difference of
0.53 × SD**, which at the observed SD of 2.5 is **1.32 surfers**. The effect under
test is about 3.3, so 30 is ample and also buys the crowd strata. Strata matter
because the one thing the 15-frame estimate could not resolve is whether the gap
grows with the crowd (r = −0.08, p = 0.77, n = 15).

## What each outcome means

- **Pass B reads high again, by about 3** — the careful protocols are right, the
  direct count misses surfers, and the crowd-dependent threshold and adaptive
  containment should be turned on.
- **The two agree** — the 11% was specific to the `spotcheck` sitting, and the
  rules stay off until there is a better reason.
- **Pass B reads high but the extra boxes are marginal** — judge that from the
  `is_surfer` = `n` rate and the notes, not from the totals. If close looking is
  manufacturing surfers it will show up as boxes you were unsure about rather
  than as a clean count difference, and that is the case for a third pass:
  blind adjudication of the disputed objects mixed with controls.

---

## Result (both passes returned, 2026-10-20)

**Outcome: "the two agree."** The direct count did not read ~11% low against
box-by-box on the same frames, so `spotcheck`'s −3.27 was not a protocol bias in
the assumed direction, and `CROWD_THRESH_SCHEDULE` /
`CONTAINMENT_DENSITY_SLOPE` **stay off**.

The paired difference ran slightly the other way, but it is inside the noise and
**should not be quoted as a measured protocol gap**: 15 of 30 frames tied, seven
frames carry the result, all of the signal is in the crowded strata (A≥20
p=0.007 vs A<20 p=0.26), and there the mean absolute difference (1.93) is the
size of the reviewer's own stated ± (2.00). 22 of 30 frames agree within that ±,
26 of 30 after the correction below, which takes the sign test to p=0.065.

So the crowd-dependence question the strata were bought for is *suggestive*
(r = −0.62 between crowd size and the gap) but confounded with the two design
flaws below, and it is not worth more hand counting to resolve — see
`PROJECT_HISTORY.md` for the power calculation and for where the detection rules
get judged instead (`eval_detector.py` against the held-out CVAT split).

### Two design flaws to fix before this is run again

1. **No column for a box covering more than one surfer.** Fifteen boxes got a
   prose note instead, and those surfers were — correctly, given nowhere to put
   them — left out of `surfers_with_no_box`. Add a `surfers_in_box` integer
   column. `reviewdays` has the same hole, which biases its historical +0.27 low.
2. **No repeat frames**, so there is no intra-rater noise floor and the
   observed SD mixes protocol effect with reviewer stochasticity. Include ~10%
   repeats, as the blind-adjudication design called for.

Also requested from the review itself: draw the boxes more transparently and
ship the clean crop alongside, so a dense cluster can be compared with and
without boxes.

### What pass B measured about the detector (independent of the comparison)

| | |
|---|---|
| box precision | **97.9%** (603 `y` of 616 judged; `B20` had no boxes) |
| recall vs surfers with no box | **92.6%** (48 missed) |
| recall counting in-box extras as misses | **90.9%** |
| detector vs box truth | **−1.13** per frame (−5.2%) |
| detector vs direct count | **−2.17** per frame (−9.5%) |
| best F1 over a confidence sweep | **0.952 at 0.195**, the production threshold |
